items.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018
items.q: Then of course we’d watch a lot of Ed Sullivan, you know, on Sunday nights.

ctx.x: Bass lines, which is why I love swing music so much, because the bass moves. It makes you, I like anything — I like to move you know. I like that, I liked Motown, because of those bass lines — those great James Jamerson bass lines. I used to wonder, when I used to watch, I used to watch a lot of variety shows growing up. I don’t know if you did the same. So I was hooked on, we’d — my mother had a radio in the kitchen so we’d listen to everything from Arthur Godfrey Hour to William B. Williams who was a DJ in New…

morning, or Tony Bennett or Dean Martin, Ella Fitzgerald, then maybe they’d be on somebody’s program at night. So it was really exciting to me. Then of course we’d watch a lot of Ed Sullivan, you know, on Sunday nights. And I would wonder sometimes like now I know why, but I would wonder okay you saw the group but then there was all this arrangement happening. Where are the other people? Where are the strings at? I hear strings. I hear horns. You know? And all I’m seeing is four guys or whatever, singing, with…
Me too. Did a time come when you, in your career, you had to lip sync for videos and stuff?
